chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad al-Katib from Amr ibn Khalid ibn Talhah al-Qannad from Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani from Simak ibn Harb from Qabus from his father from Ali: That Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding
a man and a woman who both died from the plague, dying on one bed, with the man's hand and foot on the woman, so he assigned the inheritance to the man and said, 'Indeed, he died after her.'

key_terms.فِي الشَّكِّ: in case of doubt/uncertainty (implied context of simultaneous death)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided when a husband and wife die simultaneously?
ai.summary: In this ruling from the plague era, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) applied the principle of 'presumption of seniority' (tarjih) to resolve simultaneous death, determining that the husband inherited from the wife because his death was presumed to have occurred moments later. This precedent is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for handling cases of concurrent death where the exact order is unknown, emphasizing that inheritance rights depend on the relative sequence of death rather than mere simultaneity.
